      "finding": "Level 2's title, 'Quitters spread the virus most,' is a claim the paper does not support in those words. The model's parameter values give β1 = 0.214 and β3 = 0.05, so acutely infected individuals have a per-capita transmission rate more than four times that of quitters. The paper's closest statement is that β3 'exerts the strongest influence on the reproduction number' in the independent-vari­­­­"

      "level": 2,
      "severity": "advice",
      "suggestion": "Retitle the level to reflect what the paper actually shows, e.g. 'Quitters' transmission rate and the epidemic peak' or 'How quitters' higher transmissibility shapes the outbreak.' The level's content (varying β3 and watching the quitters' peak) is valid; only the title overstates the claim."
    ,

      "finding": "Level 3's level-rule check holds on only 16 of 20 parameter combinations. The statement 'the other world's peak of quitters is lower by more than 0.003' is not guaranteed: in 4 of 20 cases the difference is ≤ 0.003. The direction (lower peak) is correct, but the numerical threshold is worded more strongly than the measurement supports across the full parameter range."
